skills.name: aswath-compact
skills.description: Use when the session's context is filling, before a long task, or when the user says "compact", "free up context", "too much in context", or asks how much context is being used. Measures what the session is actually carrying, distils it into a dense handoff file, persists that handoff so any later session can resume from it, and reports how to actually release the window.

skills.name: aswath-token-evaluator
skills.description: Use when the user asks how many tokens a session used, what the context was spent on, how much was saved, whether the token guard is working, or wants a statistics report after a session. Produces a per-session table, a cause breakdown, measured savings from blocked reads, counterfactual savings from repeat reads, and a before/after comparison around the guard.

skills.name: aswath-token-guard
skills.description: Use when the user asks why a session is expensive, how much context is being used, what is wasting tokens, where the context window went, or before a long task that would grow the window. Measures the live session, attributes every token to a cause, names the largest waste, and applies the four habits that cut it. Also the entry point when a PreToolUse hook blocks a repeat read.

skills.name: aswath-token-ledger
skills.description: Use when the user wants the raw context ledger of a session - every token attributed to a cause, the costliest tool outputs, files read more than once - or wants to compare token spend across sessions. Reads the MiniMax Code transcript store directly, including sessions that predate the token-guard hooks.

skills.name: aswath-capability
skills.description: Orchestrator that takes a whole project from a one-line brief to shipped work. Use for 'build me an ecommerce site', 'build a project', 'I want to build X', 'start a project', or any end-to-end build that spans UI, architecture, and execution. It brainstorms the brief with you, researches whether the idea will actually work, plans UI and architecture, then resolves and invokes the right skills, subagents, hooks, MCPs and plugins from the registry - authoring missing ones mid-build when a real gap appears. skills.name: aswath-commit

skills.name: aswath-forge

skills.name: aswath-throw

skills.name: aswath-talk
skills.description: [simple] How Aswath wants replies written — plain words, short sentences, no jargon walls, minimal ceremony, plus the "smallest thing that actually works" pushback. Use when the user says "aswath-talk", "talk like me", "plain english", "simpler", "too long", "i dont understand", or when a reply needs to be short and readable instead of dense. Combines caveman-style compression with ponytail-style minimalism and everyday wording.
